articles.title: Man stabbed to death after asking car occupants to drive slowly in Delhi's Shakurpur
articles.summary: New Delhi: A 27-year-old man was allegedly stabbed to death by an occupant of a car following an argument between the two sides over rash driving in Shakurpur here in the early hours of Friday, police said. After returning from a wedding function around 1 am, Yogesh, a resident of JJ Colony in Shakurpur, and his friends were standing on G-Block Road when they had an argument with the occupants of a Hyundai i20 over alleged rash driving in northwest Delhi , a senior police officer said. The altercation escalated into a violent confrontation and one of the occupants of the car allegedly pulled out a knife and stabbed Yogesh in the neck before fleeing from the spot along with others, police said. Delhi: Two teenagers stabbed to death in separate incidents The officer said Yogesh sustained a life-threatening injury and was rushed to Maharaja Agrasen Hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead. The hospital informed police, following which a team reached the spot and opened an investigation. The two sides knew each other and belonged to the same locality, the officer said. "We have identified the accused and are conducting raids to arrest them. Police have registered a case," the officer said. Police are examining the sequence of events leading to the stabbing and the roles of those present in the car. The victim's family alleged that the incident stemmed from a seemingly minor objection to the speed of the car. They demanded stringent action against those involved. Yogesh's grandmother said he had gone to attend a wedding function with his friends and was returning home when the incident occurred. She said Yogesh asked some people travelling in a car to drive slowly, after which an argument broke out between him and the occupants. "They got into a spat, and then one of them stabbed him in the neck before fleeing. He was rushed to a nearby hospital, but the doctors declared him dead," she said. Reeta said the family received the news that a person stabbed her nephew, Yogesh, late at night. "Police should arrest the accused as soon as possible," she said. Further investigation is underway, police said.

articles.title: Union Cabinet clears fresh delimitation-linked women quota bill
articles.summary: Ahead of Parliament’s special session beginning November 30, the Union Cabinet met on Friday and cleared a fresh delimitation-linked women's reservation bill, which is likely to be brought before the Parliament next week. The bill will facilitate a uniform 50 per cent rise in Lok Sabha seats in all states. Also, there will be a freeze on seats till 2051. According to a PTI report, the bill was taken up at a special meeting of the Union Cabinet, which approved amendments aimed at ensuring that no state loses its proportionate representation in the Lok Sabha following delimitation. 'No change in position, no question of any compromise': M K Stalin says DMK stands firm on demands regarding delimitation The fresh bill seeks to use the 2011 Census to redraw the increased seats. The proposed amendment seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the present 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation. The treasury benches said the move will pave the way for the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislative assemblies ahead of the 2029 general election. The meeting, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi , was held at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth. The government is keen to secure the passage of the legislation during the special sitting of Parliament, which begins on Monday. Delimitation Bill: I.N.D.I.A. bloc to seek freeze on distribution of seats for 25 years; oppose CEC Gyanesh Kumar's role The government had introduced the bill during a special session in April, but it failed to secure passage in the Lok Sabha . It has now expressed confidence that it has the required numbers to get the legislation passed. A two-thirds majority in both houses of Parliament is a must for a Constitutional amendment bill to get cleared. The PTI report said the DMK and NCP, besides BRS, are expected to support the bill. The Opposition I.N.D.I.A. bloc is against the legislation and will be meeting on Saturday to discuss its strategy. (With PTI inputs)

articles.title: Deepam row: Supreme Court orders lamp lighting on Saturday; suspends temple board
articles.summary: New Delhi: Taking a stern view of the alleged defiance of its earlier order, the Supreme Court on Friday directed that the ceremonial lamp be lit at the Deepathoon on Thiruparankundram hill on Saturday, while observing that the conduct of Tamil Nadu authorities prima facie reflected “administrative chaos” and that the situation must be dealt with an “iron hand”. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi directed that the lamp be lit using the flame from the Uchaipillaiyar Mandapam, provided it was still burning, or through any other arrangement. It further ordered that every devotee be permitted to light the lamp, maintaining a distance of at least 50 metres from the Sikandar Dargah on all sides. The court also directed the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to provide security to both the temple and the Dargah to ensure that the ceremony takes place without any disturbance. Deepam row | 'We will set right anybody trying to create constitutional chaos': Supreme Court In a significant administrative intervention, the bench suspended the Board of Trustees of the Arulmigu Subramania Swamy Temple and appointed former Madras High Court judges Justices S Vaidyanathan and V Parthiban as receivers to oversee the temple administration and ensure compliance with its directions. The directions came while the court was hearing contempt petitions alleging wilful disobedience of its November 20 order permitting the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon near the Dargah on the hilltop. Finding a prima facie case of non-compliance, the bench vacated its earlier stay on the Madras High Court's findings concerning the Deepathoon, while clarifying that the safeguards previously ordered for protecting the Dargah would continue. “There is prima facie administrative chaos in the State of Tamil Nadu, at least in Madurai District,” the bench observed. Taking exception to the apparent involvement of political considerations in the administration's response, the court remarked, “Executive authorities seem to have acted on the dictates of their political bosses.” It directed the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary to file an affidavit explaining the entire sequence of events and produce relevant communications and emails to establish how the decision not to implement the earlier order was taken. The bench also rejected the preliminary status report submitted by the Madurai District Collector, describing it as “shedding crocodile tears”. Deepam row: Tamil Nadu BJP president Nagenthran accuses ruling TVK of shifting blame on temple trustees, priests The court was particularly critical of a resolution adopted by the temple's Board of Trustees, which maintained that the lamp could be lit only at the Uchaipillaiyar Mandapam in accordance with prevailing customs and not at the Deepathoon. The Collector had relied on the resolution to justify the failure to implement the Supreme Court's direction, contending that the temple board had not authorised the ceremony. Rejecting this explanation, the bench said the resolution appeared to be an attempt to “overreach” its November 20 order through a “strained interpretation” of the directions. “The resolution on its face, firstly discloses wilful and flagrant disobedience of the interim order of this Court. Secondly, it evinces a deliberate attempt to undermine the authority of this court and the undertaking to the High Court,” the bench observed. Taking further exception to the board's suggestion that temple traditions should have been brought to the court's notice, it said the observation carried an unwarranted insinuation that the court had failed to understand the traditions despite hearing the parties in detail. The bench noted that the board had neither appeared before it nor challenged the Madras High Court's order. It held that the failure to light the lamp, read alongside the board's resolution and its invocation of tradition, prima facie disclosed “wilful and flagrant disobedience” of the court's order. The court issued show-cause notices to 13 officials and members of the temple administration, including Chief Secretary M Sai Kumar, DGP Mahesh Agarwala, Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishna, senior HR&CE officials, the Madurai Superintendent of Police and members of the temple's Board of Trustees. They have been directed to appear personally before the court on December 15. Emphasising the supremacy of the rule of law, the bench said, “Time has come to deal with such situations with an iron hand, otherwise, it will lead to constitutional chaos.” Referring to Article 144 of the Constitution, which requires all civil and judicial authorities to act in aid of the Supreme Court, the bench said no authority could treat its judicial orders as negotiable. “An order of this court is not an invitation to negotiate. It binds all authorities, until this court itself modifies,” it said. “Any attempt to pollute the stream of justice, by anyone, whosoever high, will not be tolerated,” the court cautioned, underscoring that defiance of judicial orders could not be allowed to undermine constitutional governance.

articles.title: Rupee nosedives 60 paise to settle at 92.98 against US dollar
articles.summary: Mumbai: The rupee depreciated 60 paise to settle at 92.98 (provisional) against the US dollar on Friday, paring its recent gains, amid a surge in crude oil prices and a sharp fall in domestic equity markets. The local unit was also weighed down by a strong American currency even as the inflow of foreign funds provided support, according to forex traders. In the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 92.44 and touched the day's low of 93.01 before settling at 92.98 (provisional) against the greenback, logging a steep loss of 60 paise from its previous close. On Thursday, the rupee settled down 18 paise to 92.38 against the US dollar, a day after jumping 65 paise to reach its highest level this fiscal year so far. Rupee plunges 24 paise to 92.62 against US dollar in early trade In the past seven months, the rupee became the best-performing Asian currency, recovering nearly 5 per cent from its lowest-ever close of 96.88 against the US dollar recorded on October 8. Anuj Choudhary, Research Analyst, Mirae Asset Sharekhan, said the rupee reversed gains on a sharp fall in domestic markets and a surge in crude oil prices. "Crude oil prices rose on Houthis attacking Aramco facility in Saudi Arabia. Dollar index, too, recovered from morning lows... Elevated dollar and month-end dollar demand may also pressurise the rupee," Choudhary said, adding, "USD-INR spot price is expected to trade in a range of Rs 92.65 to Rs 93.20." Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was at 103.77, higher by 0.16 per cent. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.64 per cent higher at $97.19 per barrel in futures trade. Analysts said oil prices regained above the $95-a-barrel level after reports of vessels being targeted in the Strait of Hormuz, fuelling concerns over supply-chain disruptions. "Higher crude prices have increased dollar demand from oil importers and revived inflationary concerns, putting additional pressure on the domestic currency. Despite record foreign equity inflows of $15.16 billion in November, which have provided some support to the rupee and enabled the RBI to rebuild its foreign exchange reserves, rising oil prices and geopolitical uncertainty are currently weighing on market sentiment. From a technical perspective, USD/INR resistance is placed around 93.50-94.30, while the support zone is seen at 92.00-91.00," said Kaveri More, Commodity Technical Analyst at Choice Broking. In the domestic equity market, Sensex crashed 989.33 points, or 1.17 per cent, to settle at 83,339.26, while the Nifty tumbled 277.30 points or 1.07 per cent to 25,607.20. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought equities worth Rs 5,843.33 crore on a net basis on Thursday, according to exchange data.

articles.title: Pay-As-You-Drive is More Than a Trend. Here's Why Digit Insurance Sees It as the Future of Motor Cover
articles.summary: Not every car purchased today is used for daily commute. In many urban households, one vehicle typically handles the weekday routine while another is reserved for weekend drives, family outings, shopping trips, or occasional travel . As work patterns evolve and alternative mobility options become more accessible, many vehicle owners are finding that their cars spend more time parked than on the road. Yet when insurance renewal arrives, coverage decisions are often made the same way they were years ago, without considering whether usage habits have changed. This shift in vehicle ownership and usage patterns is bringing greater attention to the Pay-As-You-Drive (PAYD) add-on in motor insurance , a usage-linked approach designed for drivers whose vehicles may not be used every day. What Pay-As-You-Drive Insurance Actually Means? Pay-As-You-Drive (PAYD) add-on is a feature for eligible vehicles that offers a discount on the Own Damage (OD) premium of a car insurance policy. The discount is provided based on the vehicle’s previous driving patterns and the applicable eligibility criteria. For eligible customers, the PAYD benefit is automatically offered during policy purchase or renewal . The discounted premium is linked to a specified kilometre limit for the policy period. If the vehicle exceeds this limit, the coverage can be extended through a top-up , subject to the policy terms and conditions. For vehicle owners whose cars are driven occasionally rather than every day, the Pay as You Drive add-on offers an alternative approach that incorporates vehicle usage into the insurance framework. As driving habits become increasingly diverse, PAYD is emerging as an option for vehicle owners whose usage patterns differ from those of traditional daily commuters. Why is PAYD Becoming Relevant for Urban Vehicle Owners? The way people use their vehicles has changed noticeably in recent years. Hybrid work arrangements, expanding metro networks, app-based mobility services, and improved public transport options have reduced the need for daily driving for many urban residents. For some households, the car that once handled everyday office commutes is now primarily used for weekend trips or occasional errands. At the same time, multi-car households are becoming more common. In such situations, one vehicle may serve as the primary mode of transport while another remains reserved for family outings, leisure travel, or special occasions. As these ownership patterns evolve, interest is growing in insurance options that can better reflect how vehicles are actually being used . What Types of Customers Can Benefit from PAYD Add-on? PAYD is not necessarily the right fit for every driver. It is generally more relevant for people whose vehicle usage remains relatively limited and predictable throughout the year. Across these profiles, the common factor is that the vehicle is not being used extensively on a daily basis . Why Flexibility Matters in a PAYD Plan? One of the realities of vehicle ownership is that usage patterns can change unexpectedly . A vehicle that starts out as a weekend car may become a frequently used family vehicle. A new job, changing family responsibilities, relocation, or lifestyle changes can all affect how often a car is driven. For this reason, vehicle owners should evaluate not only the coverage itself but also the flexibility available within the plan . As usage-based insurance continues to gain traction, insurers are increasingly focusing on flexibility alongside coverage. Companies such as Digit Insurance have introduced Pay-As-You-Drive offerings that provide vehicle owners with options designed around varying driving needs and changing usage patterns. Evaluating these features can help vehicle owners choose a solution that remains relevant even if their driving habits evolve over time. When Does PAYD Make the Most Sense? Opting for a PAYD add-on can be particularly useful in multi-vehicle households , where one car handles routine commuting while another is used primarily for leisure trips, shopping runs, or occasional travel. Similarly, remote and hybrid workers may find that their vehicles spend significantly more time parked than on the road compared to traditional office commuters. PAYD may be worth exploring when: ● The vehicle is used mainly for weekends and occasional trips . ● It serves as a secondary household car rather than the primary mode of transport. ● Annual driving patterns are relatively predictable . ● The vehicle is driven infrequently throughout most of the year . However, vehicle owners should assess their actual driving habits before making a decision. A car that is expected to remain an occasional-use vehicle may be a better fit for a usage-linked insurance option than one whose usage patterns change frequently or involve regular long-distance travel. How Are Changing Driving Habits Influencing Insurance Choices? The growing interest in PAYD reflects broader changes in how people own and use vehicles, like driving habits are reshaping insurance preferences. With many customers driving less frequently than traditional insurance models assume, there is growing demand for solutions that offer greater fairness, flexibility, and alignment between premiums and actual vehicle usage . This shift is helping drive interest in innovative models such as Pay as You Drive (PAYD) . What This Means During Car Insurance Renewal Car insurance renewal is often treated as a routine annual task. However, it can also serve as an opportunity to reassess whether existing coverage still reflects current driving habits. For owners of occasional-use vehicles, asking how frequently the car was actually driven during the previous year can be an important starting point. This evaluation can also be a useful opportunity to review broader car insurance requirements and ensure that the chosen coverage continues to align with actual vehicle usage rather than assumptions based on past driving patterns. articles.title: A Bengaluru brand rethinks the business hotel, one neighbourhood at a time.
articles.summary: For a business hotel, what deserves more space: the lobby, the bathroom or a balcony where a guest can step outside? Bengaluru-based PXL Hotels is building its answer around how people actually spend their stay. The brand, from Raja Builders & Estates, approaches hospitality through both the building and its daily use. Its premise is that thoughtful allocation of space and investment can create a distinctive experience without making every addition an expensive one. “We started by asking what a guest actually values enough to pay for. Every feature has a cost, and someone eventually pays it. If it adds little to the stay, why make the guest fund it? That question guides where we invest,” says Raja Arjun, Managing Director of Raja Builders and Founder of PXL Hotels. An architect by training, Arjun draws inspiration from Japanese compact homes, where fully equipped interiors make every inch useful. At PXL, that thinking translates into large, spacious rooms with kitchenettes, deliberately larger bathrooms and balconies. The emphasis is on making space useful rather than simply reducing it. Technology simplifies the stay, while transparent pricing keeps costs predictable. At the 24-room PXL27 near Cubbon Park, the neighbourhood connection begins with the name: PXL identifies the brand, while 27 comes from the local PIN code. Food carries that connection further. The supper club draws on local cooking, changing its menu every few months with the seasons. Returning diners encounter new dishes grounded in familiar culinary references. The café bakery takes inspiration from the everyday neighbourhood bakery, giving familiar favourites a fresh twist at accessible prices. Both draw residents into the hotel, bringing travellers into contact with the city beyond its usual visitor attractions. Dining consequently serves an audience beyond overnight guests, giving the property a place in neighbourhood routines as well as travel itineraries. According to company figures, PXL27 reached 80% occupancy within four months, against its internal benchmark of approximately 12 months for a comparable hotel to stabilise. Rakuten, HCG and BEML are among its named corporate clients. Announced projects include 100 rooms in Electronic City, 140 at Sadahalli and management takeovers covering 50 rooms in central Bengaluru. With PXL27, these total 314 operating and proposed rooms, towards an ambition of 1,000. PXL is building a robust team of veteran advisors and strengthening in-house operational capabilities as it combines new developments with existing hotel takeovers. What emerges is a business hotel shaped by its address, from its name to its food. Generous rooms accommodate the practical rhythms of a longer stay, while seasonal menus give local diners a reason to return. Together, these choices give the Bengaluru brand its own interpretation of city hospitality.

articles.title: Karunadotsava: The language row that united Karnataka — and continues to raise questions
articles.summary: The Gokak agitation of the 1980s, described as one of the biggest language-centric movements in post-independent India, had its origin in the much contested three languages formula, which was adopted on the recommendations of several education commissions. The most contentious aspect of this proposal was offering Sanskrit as the first language in Karnataka’s high schools until the Gokak movement raised a huge protest against it. Kannada writers and intellectuals join a protest in front of the M S building in Bengaluru Sanskrit was directly offered at the high school level, with the option to answer examinations in Kannada or English. Surprisingly, Sanskrit students were found to score high marks and thereby secured higher ranks in the SSLC examinations. Protestors gather at Cubbon Park in Bengaluru This led to a situation in which Kannada, the state language, was the last choice of many students, especially in the English-medium schools. Kannadiga students were not required to study their native language or mother tongue at all in high school. The then Chief Minister D Devaraj Urs took a decision to correct the anomaly by moving Sanskrit from the first language to the group of third languages, while Kannada and all languages of the land (including minority languages) were brought to the group of first and second languages. Police stop agitators at Vidhana Soudha Circle in Bengaluru The language question It has to be said emphatically that at no stage were languages other than Kannada made to lose the constitutionally assured status and protection, because the myth circulated then — which still survives — is that these languages were marginalised by the hegemony of Kannada. After Urs lost power in 1980, the new Chief Minister R Gundu Rao brought Sanskrit back to the first language group. Kannada writers and intellectuals join a protest in front of the M S building in Bengaluru Writers and hundreds of Kannada organisations began protests against the move and the government decided to constitute a committee under the chairmanship of Jnanpith awardee Prof V K Gokak to look into the issue. Interestingly, there was suspicion that the committee would favour Sanskrit and protests were held with the slogan ‘Gokak, Go Back’. However, the Gokak Committee Report (January 27, 1981) not only rejected the inclusion of Sanskrit as a first language, but went on to recommend Kannada as the sole first language at the high school level and made Kannada compulsory at the primary level from Class 3 onwards. The delay and reluctance of the state government to implement the Gokak Committee Report led to the Gokak movement, which spread across the state. Outside Kannada literary circles and organisations, the response was tepid to begin with. But the iconic actor Rajkumar’s entry turned it into a mass movement overnight. The visuals of the protests across the state provide incredible evidence of the fervor and the energy of the movement. There was also some rioting, which led to the death of seven persons in the police firing. The state government had to yield. Seminal debates In retrospect, the Gokak movement provoked seminal debates over the need for education in the mother tongue, the hegemony of English, the cultural politics involving Sanskrit and most importantly, the status of the state language vis-a-vis other mother tongues. Scholars have also seen the Gokak movement as the public manifestation of the fissures in Kannada identity. Jnanpith awardee U R Ananthamurthy misread it as “mass hysteria”. Some scholars cautioned against the movement’s vulnerability to communal discourses, linguistic hegemony and violence, as witnessed in the Cauvery and anti-Urdu riots. Changing context The legacy of the Gokak movement has to be constantly reformulated in the radically changing context of migrant labour, Bengaluru’s cosmopolitanism, and the ambivalent nature of globalisation, all set within the framework of an inclusive federalism and democracy. These complex issues were given a short shrift in the judgements of the Karnataka High Court and the constitutional bench of the Supreme Court when minority institutions and others questioned the orders passed by the state government in the aftermath of the movement. While the judgements uphold the right of the child (parent by proxy) to choose a language and medium of instruction, courts also in the hearings and obiter dicta advocated English in the language and logic of global capitalism As many Kannada writers have said, this provided an impetus to the private institutions to promote English in schools. As the Kothari Commission feared, the education system itself may perpetuate inequalities and hierarchies through such happenings. (The writer is a literary and cultural critic based in Shivamogga) This article was first published on November 25, 2020 and it has been reproduced as part of Deccan Herald's Karunadotsava 2026 campaign to celebrate Karnataka Rajyotsava.

articles.title: China’s drones are reshaping Asia’s militaries
articles.summary: By Ruth Pollard for Bloomberg Southeast Asian militaries have a modernisation problem: They cannot afford to miss the global shift toward drone warfare, particularly after Ukraine demonstrated the importance of cheap unmanned systems and rapid adaptation. And yet some of the most affordable and readily available technology comes from China — and buying it risks creating a dependency that could bring its own dangers. That leaves the governments of a $4.5 trillion bloc, collectively the world’s fourth-largest economy, trying to hedge their bets on defence hardware between Washington and Beijing, without getting caught in the slipstream of their superpower rivalry. Thailand — a formal US treaty ally — offers an interesting case study. America is a long-standing military supplier, with more than $3 billion in active sales that include F-16 fighter jet upgrades, helicopters and armoured vehicles. Still, it’s the country with the strongest Chinese defence penetration, including battle tanks, naval systems and UAV technology. Last year’s Thai-Cambodia border war, the worst ever conflict between two members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, offers a real-time indication of how a military simultaneously modernising with both US and Chinese weapons might fight. Thailand used combat aircraft imported from Sweden and the US, armed with South Korean guided bombs, alongside a locally developed drone based on Chinese technology, while Cambodia employed Chinese rocket systems. At its height, air strikes and artillery exchanges displaced over 600,000 people in Cambodia and some 400,000 in Thailand, with at least 150 killed. In China, the ‘female gaze’ is driving an entertainment boom The use of mixed arsenals is likely to become increasingly common in the region. Indonesia operates Chinese- and Turkish-made drones and is purchasing Indian cruise missiles, while the Philippines uses Israeli-made hardware and Australian-supplied systems. Both are adapting their UAV fleets for surveillance and operations in the South China Sea. Drones are also widely used by all sides in Myanmar’s civil war. Beijing’s role in Southeast Asian military modernisation frequently involves technology transfer and local development, making the Chinese origin of the eventual system much less obvious. China is now one of a small group of countries dominating the international military-drone market, along with the US, Israel, Turkey and Iran — and has been particularly important in making armed UAVs available to countries that struggled to obtain American systems. China’s importance runs deeper than the weapons it sells, though it’s worth noting that it dominates the commercial drone market, worth more than $5 billion annually. Turkey may be the world’s largest exporter of finished military drones, but those rankings obscure Beijing’s grip on the components and supply chains that increasingly underpin drone warfare. Even Ukraine, which has one of the world’s fastest-growing domestic industries, relies on China for 71% of its imports of key inputs. Everyone is rushing to buy these new systems, and unlike the West, Beijing is far less picky about who it’s selling to. Most nations opting to buy Beijing’s stack aren’t abandoning Western equipment altogether. But it’s clear that the huge boost in military spending globally is also lifting the sale of Chinese technology, said Gerald Mako, an expert on artificial intelligence and autonomous systems governance and a research affiliate at Cambridge University. The implications extend beyond the capabilities of individual weapons systems to technological dependence and the military balance across the Indo-Pacific, he told me. Since the beginning of President Donald Trump’s second term, Washington has shifted its priorities toward the Middle East through its war in Iran, and is now more interested in showy meetings with China and Russia than maintaining a stable presence in Southeast Asia. It’s overstating it to say that US military supremacy in Asia is over, however the gap with China is now narrower than ever. Explainer | How China got access to Nvidia's AI chips despite rules to stop them The Lowy Institute’s 2026 Asia Power Index found that the US-Iran conflict, combined with Washington’s pressure on countries to spend more on their own defence, had contributed to a record decline in US diplomatic influence in Asia. Nations in this part of the world are used to a US that’s distracted by priorities and conflicts elsewhere. But the collateral damage is glaringly visible this time. Iran’s move to restrict shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and disrupt fuel supplies should not be underestimated. The Philippines remains under a national energy emergency eight months after it was declared, while every Southeast Asian government has been forced to introduce emergency measures to cushion the impact of the war . China itself has important weaknesses. Its impressive pace of shipbuilding masks a key question about just how conflict-ready Beijing is. It hasn’t fought a major war since invading Vietnam in 1979 — unlike the US, which starts wars with depressing regularity. It’s too early to say whether more nations are planning to adopt China’s military systems. The impact of winder adoption would certainly be profound and long-lasting. To counter this, the US, South Korea and other exporters should push to develop more affordable systems. They must be able to integrate easily with Asia’s armed forces while ensuring sensitive data is shared securely. The US could also ease its export regulations and expand sales among nations that have struggled to access its drone technology. There are always options. But with US focus elsewhere, Southeast Asian nations may be left with only one — China — to help them modernise their militaries. (Disclaimer: The views expressed above are the author's own. They do not necessarily reflect the views of DH.)

articles.title: Karunadotsava | Lakes, parks and more — a look at Bengaluru's nature escapes
articles.summary: For some, the day begins with a walk in a nearby park, a yoga session on dew-covered grass or picking a few fresh flowers for pooja. For others, it is about visiting a garden unwind against a green backdrop and feel refreshed after a stressful day. Bengaluru , known as the Garden City, has more than a thousand parks, according to civic records. These green spaces have become an integral part of everyday life for its citizens. How many of these parks and gardens have you visited? They are not just places that add to the city's beauty; they also carry a rich history, though some have recently faced the threat of tree-felling or losing portions of their land to development projects. Cubbon Park, officially Sri Chamarajendra Park, is a major landmark and green space in Bengaluru. It was laid out in 1870 soon after the completion of the Attara Kacheri, the present Karnataka High Court building. Located in the heart of India's fastest-growing cities, it is home to more than 6,000 trees belonging to as many as 68 genera and 96 species. The park offers serene walking paths and scenic nature spots for birdwatching and photography. However, Cubbon Park has faced ongoing environmental concerns. Activists and residents have staged protests against proposed parking facilities and an art complex, fearing they could reduce the city's green space. Walkers’ association opposes coffee shop in Cubbon Park Another key feature of Bengaluru's green cover is the Lalbagh Botanical Garden. Commissioned by Hyder Ali in 1760 and later developed by his son Tipu Sultan, the garden is home to more than 1,850 species of plants from across the world. It also serves as a centre for botanical research, horticultural education and plant conservation. Lalbagh hosts bi-annual flower shows, drawing thousands of visitors. Other attractions include Lalbagh lake, the famous Peninsular Gneiss rock and the Bonsai Garden. Lalbagh has also seen protests over development projects. Recently, more than 5,000 people gathered at the garden to oppose the proposed Hebbal–Silk Board tunnel road project and the latest amendments to the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act. Led by veteran environmental activist A N Yellappa Reddy, citizens held a 'rock-hugging' protest. The Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, was born out of a simple idea: protecting parks like Lalbagh and Cubbon Park, which are considered Bengaluru’s green jewels. The Act has undergone seven amendments so far. The latest amendment allowed utilising up to 5% of park land for infrastructure projects. Following the public opposition, the State Cabinet decided to withdraw the amendment. ‘Save Lalbagh’ cry grows louder as thousands rally against Parks Amendment Bill Bengaluru may be known as the Garden City, but its blue cover is equally noteworthy. Ulsoor Lake (also known as Halasuru Lake) is one of Bengaluru's oldest and largest lakes. Built by Kempe Gowda II in the 1600s, it spreads across around 50 hectares and features several small islands. The historic lake recently underwent maintenance work and was temporarily closed to the public. Jakkur Lake, spread across approximately 160 acres, is located in north Bengaluru. It is known for its constructed wetland, which supports the growth of aquatic plants. Another prominent waterbody, Sankey Tank is an artificial lake and a popular spot for walking, jogging and picnics. However, it has seen growing concerns over its ecological health. Residents and environmental groups have raised issues such as excessive concretisation, sewage inflow, falling water levels and the impact of unplanned development around the lake. The city is home to many more lakes and waterbodies, each with its own history and features. Summit explores Karnataka’s growing green foot print Adding to the city's popular parks and lakes are several historic and sprawling temples where devotees can walk through tree-lined paths to reach the shrine and spend time within the spacious premises, which also feature waterbodies and plenty of greenery. These include the Kadu Malleshwara Temple, the Guruvayoorappan Temple near Nettigere Gate on Kanakapura Road, and Trimurti Temple and Trimurti Adyatma Mandira.

articles.title: Nestle India receives Rs 36.36 lakh EPFO demand
articles.summary: New Delhi: FMCG major Nestle India on Friday said it has received a demand of Rs 36.36 lakh from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) , including damages and a penalty of over Rs 20 lakh for the period 2012-2019. The order has been issued by the Regional Office of EPFO, Mysuru, under section 7Q and 14B of the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, the company said in a regulatory filing. "The company has received an order from the Regional Office of Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation demanding an amount of Rs 36,36,548, which includes an amount of Rs 20,09,516 on account of damages/penalty for the period of 2012-2019 under PF Code," it said. Employees' Provident Fund Organisation cuts minimum PF balance requirement to 10% from 25% The order, received by the company on November 26, 2026, has no material impact on its financials, operations or other activities, the filing added. Under Section 7Q of the EPF Act, an employer is liable to pay interest on amounts due under the Act, while Section 14B empowers the EPFO to recover damages in the form of a penalty in cases of default in payment of provident fund contributions and other statutory dues. Nestle India is one of the country's leading food and beverage companies, with brands including Maggi, Nescafe, KitKat, Milkmaid and Everyday in its portfolio. Shares of Nestle India were trading at Rs 1,316.90 on BSE during the afternoon, down 0.29 per cent from the previous close.

articles.title: Two-thirds of Indian adolescents have vitamin B12 deficiency: ICMR survey
articles.summary: New Delhi: Nearly two-thirds of Indian adolescents have vitamin B12 deficiency, with the prevalence marginally higher among boys than girls, according to findings of a national survey conducted by the ICMR -National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN). The survey found vitamin B12 deficiency in 66.1 per cent of adolescent boys aged 10-19 years and 65.4 per cent of girls in the same age group. Deficiency was defined as a serum vitamin B12 level below 203 pg/mL. The findings are part of the Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA), conducted during 2023-25 to generate national estimates of anaemia and micronutrient deficiencies across different stages of life. Over 50% Indian women of reproductive age are anaemic: ICMR The survey covered more than 2 lakh people across 183 districts in 35 states and Union Territories and over 81,000 households. More than 1.7 lakh blood samples were analysed, according to the ICMR-NIN factsheet. Among adolescent girls, vitamin B12 deficiency was more prevalent than iron or folate deficiency. While 65.4 per cent had low vitamin B12 levels, 36.3 per cent had iron deficiency, and 8.6 per cent had folate deficiency. Among adolescent boys, 66.1 per cent had vitamin B12 deficiency, compared with 10 per cent with iron deficiency and 6.3 per cent with folate deficiency. The survey found that vitamin B12 deficiency was not limited to adolescents. It was reported in 55.2 per cent of non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 20-59 years and 57.4 per cent among women of reproductive age (15-49 years). Among adult men aged 20-59 years, the prevalence stood at 60.4 per cent. It was 41.2 per cent among women aged 60 years and above and 46.8 per cent among men in the same age group. Vitamin B12 deficiency was also recorded in 63.1 per cent of pregnant women and 51.8 per cent of lactating women. The survey indicated that the problem begins early in life, with vitamin B12 deficiency reported in 37.3 per cent of children aged 12-59 months and 46.5 per cent of those aged 5-9 years. The findings also highlighted the difference between micronutrient deficiencies and anaemia. Among adolescent girls, anaemia was reported in 46.3 per cent, while vitamin B12 deficiency affected 65.4 per cent. Among boys, the prevalence of anaemia was 22.8 per cent, compared with 66.1 per cent having vitamin B12 deficiency. The ICMR-NIN factsheet said SAMPADA provides nationally representative estimates of micronutrient deficiencies across the life course and can help identify nutritional gaps and priority groups for targeted interventions.

articles.title: SC orders lamp to be lit at Thiruparankundram Deepathoon on Nov 28, suspends temple trustees
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday suspended the board of trustees of the Thiruparankundram temple in Madurai district and ordered that the Karthigai Deepam be lit at the disputed pillar or Deepathoon on Saturday, November 28, after its earlier order was not carried out. A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi appointed former High Court judges Justice S Vaidyanathan and Justice V Parthipan as receivers to administer the temple, according to the Live Law. They have to ensure that the lamp is lit, using the flame at Uchipillaiyar. The Supreme Court has also handed over the security of the entire hill to the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), citing the failure of the Tamil Nadu Police to implement its orders. The court has directed CRPF to ensure the peaceful functioning of the temple and the Dargah. A Siva temple and the Uchi Pillaiyar temple are located on the lower part of the Tirupurakundram hill, while the dargah stands at its summit. For decades, the customary Karthigai Deepam has been lit near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple by the temple management. In 2025, however, Hindutva groups went to court demanding that the lamp be lit on the ‘deepathoon’, a stone pillar located at the hilltop, about 50 metres from the dargah. The DMK government did not implement the court’s order, and the new TVK government has followed the same course, this time citing the temple Devasthanam’s decision. The Supreme Court strongly criticised the Tamil Nadu government for not lighting the Karthigai Deepam at the pillar on November 24, as said in its earlier order. The court called the non-compliance a “flagrant violation and disobedience” and directed that the lamp be lit at the controversial site before the end of the ongoing Karthigai month. The court permitted every devotee to light it at the disputed site, at least 50 metres from the nearby dargah on all sides. It also directed the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to protect the dargah and ensure that its visitors are not obstructed or prevented from praying. The bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice Vipul Pancholi was hearing the contempt petitions against the Madurai District Collector and other authorities, along with applications seeking permission to light the lamp at the Deepathoon on another day during the month. The Supreme Court has also directed the state’s Chief Secretary to appear in person before it in connection with the non-compliance of its November 20 order. The court has also issued contempt notices to the Director General of Police, HR&CE Secretary and Commissioner, Madurai District Collector, Commissioner of Police, Superintendent of Police, temple authorities and others. “The orders of the court can’t be diluted by whoever he or she is. If anybody is attempting to create a constitutional chaos, we will set it right,” Justice Aravind Kumar observed. “An order of this court is not an invitation to negotiation until the court itself modifies it. Therefore, when the order is flouted, we can't sit in silos,” the court said in its order, according to Live Law. The court said that the decision of the temple trustees who passed a resolution to light the lamp at the Uchi Pillayar temple was a “serious infraction”. The Supreme Court had, on November 20, permitted a restricted team authorised by the temple administration to light the lamp at the Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time measure. The lamp was instead lit at the customary location near the Uchi Pillaiyar temple. The Madurai Collector’s report said the administration had made arrangements, but the ceremony could not proceed because the temple’s Board of Trustees had not authorised a team. In a preliminary status report filed before the Supreme Court on November 25, the Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishna told the Supreme Court that he made every effort to implement the court’s order permitting the lighting at the stone pillar near the Sikandar Badusha Dargah atop Thiruparankundram hill, but the temple’s Board of Trustees did not authorise a team to carry out the ceremony. Why was the lamp not lit at Thiruparankundram’s disputed pillar? What the Collector told SC “The Collector wants us to believe that he did everything. A plea was taken to the High Court against prohibitory orders passed. The Board of Trustees came from nowhere and passed the resolution. The trustees were political appointees," said Senior Advocate Guru Krishnakumar, appearing for a devotee said during the hearing. “Mandamus issued to do it on November 24 in a certain manner. Duties were parcelled out to everyone, State administration. ASI was included in the mandamus,” Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the ASI, said. “The ASI team was stopped at the dargah entrance point. Police were in control. The ASI team was asked to leave by the police and the ASI team remained on standby. They later descended the hill without examining the stone pillar,” he added. “This is a case of aggravated contempt and administrative arrogance. The state government had said ‘come what may, we will not allow the lighting of the lamp [on the stone pillar]’,” he said. Tushar Mehta has also demanded to constitute an agency like a former Supreme Court judge along with a central force to comply with the court order. Senior Advocate Saideepak Iyer, appearing for another petitioner, said the trustees were appointed by the state a week before the Supreme Court order. “Trustees are employees of the state. They were appointed only on November 13, a week before the SC order. They were state appointees and convenient shoulders from which the state could fire,” he said. Senior Advocate P Valliappan said the Ministers had made statements even before November 24, that the lamp would not be lit at the stone pillar. “We have time till December 15, let them light the lamp on any day,” he said. Senior Advocate Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the Collector said the district administration has done everything necessary to comply with the order. “Hearing must be first held on whether there was prima facie contempt at all. Then the question of purging arises. We have done all that is necessary to comply,” he said. He added the Collector was only directed to make all the arrangements and facilities for lighting the lamp and could not have done the religious act of lighting it.

articles.title: MP Played Significant Role in Making of Constitution: CM Dr. Yadav
articles.summary: Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav said that Constitution Day Celebrations 2026 reflect our glorious heritage and traditions. Equality and fraternity are the soul of our Constitution, and Madhya Pradesh played a significant role in its making. He said Madhya Pradesh made an important contribution to the decision to name the country ‘Bharat’ instead of ‘India’. Seth Shri Govind Das and Shri Hari Vishnu Kamath, who represented the Madhya Bharat region, strongly advocated the name Bharat in place of India. Madhya Pradesh also played an important role in opposing the suspension of Fundamental Rights. Chief Minister Dr. Yadav recalled that Dr. Harisingh Gour had emphasised in 1921 the need to establish a Supreme Court within the country to ensure that the highest judicial decisions were delivered in India. In 1928, Pandit Motilal Nehru also supported this view. Former Chief Ministers of Madhya Pradesh, Pandit Ravishankar Shukla and Bhagwant Rao Mandloi, among others, raised issues concerning the contributions of the States and the Centre, as well as the distribution of taxes. In the present era, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has strengthened the system through the implementation of GST, introducing a simplified framework in coordination with the States. The Chief Minister also highlighted Madhya Pradesh’s connection with the national emblem of India, the Ashoka Pillar with its four lions. Late Pandit Dinanath Bhargava played an important role in illustrating the Constitution. Chief Minister Dr. Yada further said that Madhya Pradesh has passed the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in the Legislative Assembly. The issue was first raised by Rajkumari Amrit Kaur. Equal civil rights require that matters such as marriage, divorce and succession should not be viewed on religious grounds. In the spirit of ‘One Nation, One Law and One Head’, several State governments have taken steps towards implementing the UCC under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Modi. One day, Parliament will also pass the Uniform Civil Code. The Chief Minister was addressing the Constitution Day celebrations organised at the Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly premises. Preamble of the Constitution recited collectively Chief Minister Dr. Yadav and Speaker of the Legislative Assembly Shri Narendra Singh Tomar garlanded the statue of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the architect of the Constitution, on the Assembly premises. Attempts were also made to curtail the powers of the judiciary. During the Emergency, restrictions were imposed on the country's distinguished press and media, as well as on freedom of expression. The soul of the Constitution lies in democracy, equal rights and the empowerment of weaker sections. Governments are working towards these objectives. The Opposition may disagree on any issue, but no one has been given the right to create anarchy. While I.N.D.I.A bloc parties' floor leaders in Parliament will be present, non-I.N.D.I.A bloc Opposition parties such as the DMK, the AAP and the BJD, among others, have also been invited for the meeting, they said. Meanwhile, the Congress has asked its MPs to reach New Delhi by November 29, a day before the Lok Sabha reconvenes. A special sitting of Parliament has been convened from November 30 to transact "essential" business, amid indications that the government may reintroduce a constitutional amendment for early implementation of women's reservation that involves delimitation. The move comes a day after the government proposed a special sitting of Parliament to transact "essential" business, amid indications that the delimitation-linked constitution amendment bill for early implementation of the women's quota law may be reintroduced. In a statement, Stalin said that the DMK is firm on the demands of a 7.18 per cent share of seats and proportion of representation. "No change in position, no compromise, the DMK will never compromise on Tamil Nadu's interests; nor will it depart from its principles," the party chief asserted on the expected delimitation move of the Centre. articles.summary: Lucknow: The Congress will accept a seat-sharing arrangement with the Samajwadi Party for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections only if it is "respectable and acceptable", the party's working president Imran Masood said on Friday, barely a day after party chief Mallikarjun Kharge's ''work more, talk less'' advice to him. Speaking to PTI over the phone from Delhi amid rumours of the Congress asking for 105 more seats to contest, Masood said he had already made his position clear to the Congress leadership and was putting forward his demands accordingly. "We already contested 107 seats in 2017. An alliance deal should be respectable and acceptable. Otherwise, let there be no alliance. We will not compromise on our self-respect. They have their respect, and we have ours too. It cannot happen at the cost of our self-respect," he said. Masood's remarks came a day after Kharge visited the Uttar Pradesh capital on Constitution Day, amid ongoing seat-sharing negotiations between the two INDIA bloc allies and reports of growing differences over the number of constituencies to be contested by the Congress. UP Assembly Elections 2027 | 'Alliance partner or servant?': Congress MP Masood hits out at SP amid seat-sharing talks During his Lucknow speech, Kharge had made clear that the alliance between the Samajwadi Party and the Congress was aimed at thwarting the BJP and advised Masood to "work more, talk less". Asked to comment on Kharge's advice for him, Masood said, "Kharge sahib has praised me. I am also saying that the alliance is there.But it cannot be at the cost of our self-respect." In a separate interaction with PTI Videos in Delhi, Masood hit back at Samajwadi Party leaders who had reportedly dismissed his remarks, saying that only the party leadership would decide the seat-sharing arrangement. "I don't need certificates from Samajwadi Party leaders. They should keep their wisdom to themselves. I am fighting for my party and will continue to speak and fight for my party," he said. Questioning the viability of the 26 seats reportedly offered to the Congress, he asked whether the Samajwadi Party had applied the winnability criterion while selecting those constituencies. "Why should we contest unviable seats? You can contest them yourself. Of the 26 seats, if you have said six are for us, you can contest the remaining 20. Why are you trying to give us unviable seats?" he said. Masood said the Congress is willing to contest the seats offered to it but wanted constituencies where its candidates had a genuine chance of winning. "If we are saying that we will take the seats, we also want good seats. We cannot be expected to accept whatever you decide and take the entire responsibility of defeating the BJP upon ourselves while surrendering our own interests," he said. He also called for honesty in the alliance negotiations, saying that if the two parties wanted to fight the BJP together, they should ensure adequate political space for each other. The Samajwadi Party is understood to have offered 26 seats to the Congress so far, while the latter has been seeking more than 100 seats for the 2027 polls. Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav had recently told an HT Leadership Summit in Delhi that the Congress had sought 181 seats during the initial round of discussions, adding that a seat-sharing arrangement could be worked out on the basis of the winnability of candidates. On Thursday, senior Samajwadi Party leader Shivpal Yadav had said that 26 seats had been offered to the Congress, while the remaining constituencies were being finalised through discussions between the two parties. The two parties are seeking to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections together against the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance, which is aiming to retain power in the politically crucial state, even as the first round of talks for seat-sharing remained inconclusive.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina has become 'thorn' in Bangladesh-India ties, says minister Humaiun Kobir
articles.summary: Dhaka: Sheikh Hasina has become a "thorn" in Bangladesh-India relations, with New Delhi beginning to realise the strain her presence in the country is causing to bilateral ties, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir has said. Comparing the deposed prime minister to an unwelcome guest who suddenly walks into someone's home, Kobir said India is in a difficult position as it could neither send her away nor avoid dealing with her presence, news portal bdnews24 reported. "Hasina has become a thorn in Bangladesh-India relations," he told reporters at the foreign ministry on Thursday. Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs: Humaiun Kobir India says Hasina's plan to return to Bangladesh separate from extradition request “She has become an irritation, and they understand that this is a problem for the relationship,” Kobir said. His remarks came a day after India refrained from commenting on Hasina's plan to return to Bangladesh on December 16. External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal on Wednesday said that her voluntary return should be treated separately from Dhaka's extradition request, which New Delhi is examining through established legal processes. Kobir reiterated that Hasina could return only under the extradition treaty between India and Bangladesh , either in handcuffs or under strict surveillance. "She is a criminal. There is one policy for criminals and another for ordinary citizens. She falls under the criminal category. She will come only through the extradition treaty. It is not a matter of her returning; she will be handed over,” he said. Hasina's presence in India has emerged as a contentious issue in bilateral ties since her departure from Bangladesh. She faces serious legal challenges in her home country, including a death sentence handed down in absentia by a special tribunal over the deadly crackdown on protesters during the uprising in 2024. Hasina has denied wrongdoing and questioned the legitimacy of the proceedings. Her spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali on Tuesday said that the 79-year-old ousted premier plans to return home on December 16, the day the country celebrates its victory over Pakistan in the 1971 Liberation War. Hasina, the daughter of Bangladesh's founding leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, ruled the country for 15 years before her ouster. India had enjoyed close relations with Hasina during her 15 years in power and hoped that the formation of a new government in Bangladesh would provide an opportunity to reset ties, which deteriorated sharply after her ouster. However, since taking office in February, Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman is yet to visit India despite an invitation. He skipped the BRICS summit hosted by India in September.

Tata Sons: The rules, the rift and what happens next
articles.summary: The battle to lead India's Tata Sons , the owner of marquee brands such as Jaguar Land Rover and Tetley Tea, headed for court on Friday after the sprawling conglomerate flouted the wishes of its controlling charity arm to reappoint the chairman. Tata Trusts holds a stake of 66% in Tata Sons, but the latter's board re-appointed chairman N. Chandrasekaran and has decided to pursue a possible stock market listing, putting the power struggle at the centre of the standoff. It is the second such fight in a decade for one of India's oldest and most reputed business houses, after a years-long legal battle over Tata Sons' decision to remove earlier chairman Cyrus Mistry ended in the Supreme Court upholding the decision. Here is how the current fight could play out, along with views of both sides and the complex structures, according to people familiar with the matter: TRUSTS WANT CHANDRASEKARAN OUT OF KEY DECISIONS Two of the seven charitable trusts that control Tata Sons asked the Mumbai high court on Thursday to declare Chandrasekaran's reappointment 'invalid, illegal, null and void', copies of internal memos reviewed by Reuters showed. They also seek court directions that key decisions by Tata Sons require complete support from the charity arm. Reuters has learnt the trusts will tell the court that the board should not have proceeded with the decision as both trust nominees did not back the chairman's reappointment. At Friday's hearing, the trusts are expected to ask for a halt to plans for a November 30 board meeting set to decide next steps towards listing if the chief of the charity arm and family head Noel Tata, as trust nominee, does not vote in favour. The board of Tata Sons agrees to the stock market listing, ordered by the central bank, but the charity arm does not. Tata Trusts moves Bombay High Court against reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman of Tata Sons COURT CASE FOLLOWS BITTER PUBLIC DEBATE Both sides have hired top lawyers to defend them and explain who can call the shots. Lawmaker and Congress party leader Abhishek Manu Singhvi is representing the Tata Trusts led by Noel Tata. Singhvi has previously said the dispute is about shareholder supremacy and the conglomerate cannot act like a "runaway board" independent of the controlling shareholder. That position is disputed by Tata Group's Chandrasekaran, who has roped in Harish Salve, a former solicitor general of India who often represented the government in global forums. In television remarks Salve has said the board's decision was in line with internal governing rules, urging the charity arm to get past the "I control the trusts, I control this group mindset." WHY CAN'T THE TRUSTS CALL A SHAREHOLDER MEETING AND OUST THE CHAIRMAN? The Tata Trusts have problems of their own that weaken their influence. Formed of several affiliated charities, they could have used their voting power to call for a shareholders' meeting to effectively oust Chandrasekaran. But a regulator has barred one of the main charities, the Sir Ratan Tata Trust, from convening its own meetings in a dispute over internal appointments. The charity arm says Noel Tata's opposition to the reappointment was sufficient to halt the decision. It believes such decisions cannot be made in the absence of support of a majority of the trusts' two board nominees. You will know on the floor of the Lok Sabha," Sule said in response to repeated queries on the party's stand over the delimitation bill. She said she had not received any invitation for any meeting so far. Sule maintained that it was difficult to comment without seeing the document in hand. "Until the bill comes in hand, how can I tell?... I haven't even received the syllabus. So only after getting the syllabus can I say something," she said. The NCP (SP) on Friday issued a whip directing all its eight Lok Sabha MPs to remain present in the House from November 30 during the special session of Parliament. articles.title: India vs New Zealand | Prasidh Krishna becomes the latest 'fall guy' of selection gaffe
articles.summary: Christchurch: First it was workhorse Mohammed Siraj who was the fall guy for the team management’s decision to play the inexperienced and seemingly underprepared Anshul Kamboj for the opening Test against New Zealand last week. Now Prasidh Krishna has become the victim, and for no fault of his, as the think tank opted to play Gurnoor Brar for the second Test that started at Hagley Oval on Friday. While skipper Shubman Gill said the main reason for dropping his ‘close friend’ Siraj was his poor performance in the two-Test series against Sri Lanka, it’s pretty certain even he and coach Gautam Gambhir would find it hard to give a legitimate and logical response on why they benched Prasidh for the series decider and handed Brar a Test debut. The only defence could be younger Brar is taller than Prasidh and possesses more pace. India vs New Zealand | Visitors fail to press home the advantage on Day 1 at Christchurch as Kiwis reach 246/5 The 30-year-old, a tall hit-the-deck bowler, often gets unfair flak from certain sections of the media and fans for being expensive. But what they do not understand is the Karnataka pacer was just following team orders. He is the one guy who is entrusted with doing the dirty job of bowling lines and lengths outside his comfort zone, which cannot be told to senior pros. And Prasidh does them as told without any complaint, even at the risk of being unjustly slammed in certain quarters who have little idea what is happening. Let us take three examples from his 10-Test career. In Leeds against England last year, Prasidh was asked to consistently bowl short by the think tank as they thought that could be a strategy to get the hosts’ batters out. Despite that ploy coming a cropper as England batters easily carted him for boundaries on a flat and dry pitch, Prasidh was asked to stick to the short stuff. As a result, his economy was 6.40 in the first innings and 6.13 in the second. Thankfully, the management defended him, saying he did exactly what was told to him. Prasidh was instructed to dish out the same in the first innings of the second Test in Birmingham before the management decided the experiment was failing on another flat pitch and allowed him to bowl his usual stuff in the second. From conceding 5.53 runs an over in the first, Prasidh gave away just 2.78 in the second. Then, for no fault of his, Prasidh was dropped for the next two Tests, and Kamboj was handed a debut in Manchester. But when Kamboj got cooked badly and India needed to win the final Test to level the series, they brought back Prasidh, who shone with four wickets in each of the two innings. India vs New Zealand | Preferring Anshul Kamboj over Mohammed Siraj, a decision that defies logic In the opening Test at Wellington, on another flat pitch that was condemned widely, Prasidh was asked to bowl a tad fuller in the hope that the ball would swing. But with hardly any swing or seam movement on offer, he leaked runs at the start, which is when the management asked him to revert to his usual good-length deliveries. Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak even told the media that it was purely the team’s decision to ask Prasidh to bowl at the cost of leaking runs as they looked at ways to skittle out New Zealand. Prasidh, in fact, bowled well on a lifeless track in the second innings, picking up 2/23 in 19 overs. This time too, just for following team orders, Prasidh is banished to the bench. Unfair, totally. But what is bad is the differing yardstick the management has for players. Siraj is dropped after a ‘poor’ series. Prasidh was not picked for doing things as told. But when questioned over Kamboj’s repeated failures, bowling coach Morne Morkel insisted that it is not fair to judge a bowler on two games. So then why does not it apply for Prasidh, or even Siraj? Scratch the surface and see a little deeper; the answer may lie there.

The apex court asked the Punjab and Haryana High Court to decide his plea for regular bail in two weeks from today and said the gravity of the offence can be taken to a logical conclusion in the trial. “We have not expressed any observations on the merits of the case,” the CJI said and disposed of the plea. The AAP leader had contested the Delhi Assembly elections from Vishwas Nagar constituency and taken on organisational roles in Delhi, Goa, and Maharashtra. The plea, filed through lawyer Rajat Bhardwaj, had sought setting aside of the Punjab and Haryana High Court's refusal of bail. According to the plea, the ED arrested him eight years after the original FIR, with no fresh evidence and no permission from the trial court. Singla challenged the high court's September 9 order dismissing his regular bail plea under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). The plea sought interim bail while the appeal is pending and said he was not an accused in the CBI's main case. He was also not named in the ED's 2019 ECIR, its July 20, 2022 prosecution complaint or its September 1, 2025 supplementary complaint, it said.

Deepam row | 'We will set right anybody trying to create constitutional chaos': Supreme Court
articles.summary: New Delhi: The ASI told the Supreme Court on Friday that the Tamil Nadu government committed "aggravated contempt" by not allowing its officials to go near the Karthigai Deepam at the disputed Deepathoon pillar , with the top court making it clear that its orders could not be diluted. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said it would set right anybody trying to create constitutional chaos. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Archaeological Survey of India, told the bench that the ASI was informed by the temple trustees that no instruction regarding their entry was received from higher officials. "The ASI team was halted at a certain point by the local police at 3 pm and was not permitted to go near the lamp," Mehta said. Deepam row: Supreme Court says will not hear main matter, to confine to non-compliance of Nov 20 order "My respectful submission is... this is a case of aggravated contempt and administrative arrogance. The government has been opposing from the beginning," the SG said. Mehta submitted that the lamp should be lit at Deepathoon before the contemnors were heard. "My request on behalf of the ASI is that, in view of the admitted position that the order is not complied with. Before the contemnors are heard, they should purge themselves of contempt by ensuring the lamp is lit. "The way in which police had functioned leaves nothing to be said. There are videos available which show the entire premises was packed by police. My request is please ensure that ... (some) other agency monitors this," he said. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the Madurai Collector, contradicted Mehta's submission and said that ASI officials were consulted and multiple meetings were held with them. He said the top court should first decide whether any prima facie contempt was committed. Senior advocate Sidharth Luthra, appearing for the Madurai Police Commissioner, told the court that over 5,000 personnel were deployed to ensure no breach of law and order took place and prohibitory orders were passed. "We will see whether you are shedding real or crocodile tears," the bench told the Madurai Police Commissioner. As the hearing commenced, the top court clarified that it would not go into the main matter and would confine itself to the non-compliance of its November 20 order permitting the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon as a one-time measure on November 24. The court was hearing contempt petitions and other applications on the controversy surrounding the non-lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the disputed Deepathoon pillar. Senior advocate S Guru Krishna Kumar, appearing for contempt petitioner Karthikeyan, submitted that the Tamil Nadu government had decided at the outset that it would not permit the lighting of the lamp and the preliminary report submitted by them was like a confession. "The Collector was also to consult the ASI in this regard. The onus has been completely let down. The preliminary report is like a confession. They did everything except for the lamp being lit. The only reason is the board of trustees not giving permission. The board has never contested the matter. They are bound by the order of the court," he said. The hearing is underway. On Wednesday, the Tamil Nadu government apologised to the top court over the non-lighting of the ceremonial lamp at Deepathoon and blamed the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple authorities for it. Despite the apex court's permission, the Karthigai Deepam was lit only at its customary Uchipillayar mandapam at Thirupparankundram on November 24 and not at Deepathoon.

articles.title: Opposition parties slam Union govt's move to push delimitation Bill in Parliament
articles.summary: Opposition leaders across state and party lines have slammed the Union government’s move to convene a special sitting of Parliament on November 30 to push through the proposed delimitation Bill, warning that the exercise could undermine democratic representation and alter the country’s political balance. The move was defeated once before, in April 2026, when the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led government tabled the Constitution (131st amendment) Bill to expand the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to 850 members. This was during a special session convened while election campaigns were underway in several states. With the political atmosphere having changed since the election results were declared, the BJP hopes to get the required two-thirds majority of those present and voting. Even as opposition parties, including the Congress, remain steadfastly opposed to the proposed delimitation Bill, the stance taken by regional parties such as the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) will prove crucial to the BJP government. DMK awaits delimitation bill draft, wary of BJP’s assurances on 50% seat increase Responding to the development, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)’s Rajya Sabha MP Manoj Kumar Jha alleged that the proposed delimitation exercise raised concerns about politically motivated gerrymandering in the country. “The deeper concern is the possibility of politically motivated gerrymandering, carried out to suit the whims and electoral interests of Narendra Modi ji and Amit Shah ji, along the lines of what was witnessed in Assam. Such an exercise, if driven by partisan considerations rather than constitutional principles and democratic fairness, could seriously undermine representative democracy, federal balance and national unity. Aren’t you worried?” he wrote on X. Congress veteran P Chidambaram called the BJP government’s linking of women’s reservation in Parliament to the delimitation exercise as malicious and mischievous. “The Constitution (106th) Amendment Act inserted Article 334A which tied women's reservation to delimitation after the next Census … Congress and other Opposition parties opposed the insertion of Article 334A which, unnecessarily, created two hurdles: Census and Delimitation after the Census. But the BJP was adamant and insistent on Article 334A. Mischievously. Maliciously. The Bill was passed and became a law including Article 334A. All that the BJP has to do is propose to delete Article 334A. Once Article 334A is deleted, women's reservation can be implemented immediately,” his X post read. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Sagarika Ghosh questioned the Union government’s earnestness in implementing women’s reservation in Parliament, which is a legislation that has been tied to the delimitation exercise. “If Modi-(Amit Shah) were serious about representation of women, why has the law for women’s reservation — ALREADY UNANIMOUSLY PASSED in 2023—not been implemented? The Delimitation Bill is nothing but a SHAMELESS POWER GRAB wrapped in a sari. It not only reveals the (BJP India)’s contempt for democracy, but also the BJP’s hatred and contempt for women,” she alleged. Sagarika also raised questions about whether 20 TMC MPs who defected following the party’s defeat in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections would be allowed to vote on the Bill. “For 6 months (the Lok Sabha Speaker) has NOT RULED on the 20 TRAITOR TMC MPs against whom Disqualification Petitions are pending. Even Supreme Court directives have gone unheeded. Will these traitors now be allowed to vote on the Delimitation Bill in the Lok Sabha? Are their votes legal? How can they vote when they should have been disqualified by now?” she questioned. Referring to the defections by opposition party MPs, Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said the Modi government has pinned its hopes on a “super-tainted” majority. “...[A]fter 105 days of Operation Lotus, the Modi Govt announces a special session, hoping that it will get its super-tainted two-thirds majority to pass a Constitution amendment bill. Can there be a great insult to and assault on the Constitution? The fight is on,” he stated . Stating that the Congress will not let the delimitation law pass in Parliament, Congress leader KC Venugopal accused the Union government of attempting “Sansad chori”. He said , “They are Vote Chors . They are Seat Chors . There is no doubt that their Delimitation Bill will be nothing more than an exercise in Sansad Chori .” “‘Delimitation’ will prove to be the biggest mistake in the BJP’s politics,” said Akhilesh Yadav, leader of the Samajwadi Party (SP). His state of Uttar Pradesh, which is slated to go to polls in 2027, is expected to have the highest increase in Lok Sabha seats with the delimitation exercise. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and MP Sanjay Raut called delimitation a conspiracy by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). In an X post, he said , “Delimitation is a BJP conspiracy to strip the people of this country of their power. Anyone who supports it is betraying the people of this country. They will be known as the biggest traitors of the 21st century. Therefore, every patriotic, democratic party should reject delimitation in Parliament. History always remembers the names of traitors, explanations for betrayal fade into thin air.”
